papers_read.title_as_printed: Benchmarking parametric models of disease progression for early detection of cognitive decline (Platero, Bengoa; Comput Methods Programs Biomed 2026)
Predictive value of ATN biomarker profiles in estimating disease progression in Alzheimer's disease dementia (Ezzati et al.; Alzheimers Dement 2021, author manuscript)

what_each_reports.P-33: 1163 ADNI participants (536 stable CU, 114 progressive CU, 513 stable MCI; MCI participants who progressed to dementia or reverted were excluded). Disease progression models fitted to neuropsychological scores (CDRSB, ADAS13, MMSE, etc.), with a Bayesian-KDE classifier assigning CU vs MCI status at each visit: best test-set AUC 0.96 (Leaspy, Table 2). The target transition is CU to MCI.
what_each_reports.P-192: 415 ADNI-GO/2 amnestic MCI participants with amyloid PET, CSF p-tau and FDG PET. Models trained on CN vs dementia and applied to MCI to predict incident dementia: RUSBoost on the biomarker set gives PPV 68% at 4 years against an observed 4-year conversion of 22.2% (sensitivity 61.5%, specificity 91.7%); clinical-feature RUSBoost PPV 67.3%. No AUC is reported in the main text.

quantity_a: Per-visit ROC-AUC for classifying clinical status as CU vs MCI (the CU-to-MCI transition) from neuropsychological disease-progression scores, in CU and stable-MCI ADNI participants.
quantity_b: Positive predictive value, at a 4-year horizon, for conversion from amnestic MCI to dementia, from biomarker (or clinical) features, at the cohort's natural conversion rate of 22.2%.
incompatible_if_same: No. An AUC of 0.96 and a PPV of 68% are not on the same scale: PPV depends on prevalence and threshold, AUC on neither, so the 0.28 'gap' carries no information about disagreement. Neither paper claims a result about the other's endpoint.

gates.task: mismatch: P-33's contested AUC is for CU vs MCI status (onset of MCI), P-192 predicts MCI-to-dementia conversion; the record codes both T2 but the transitions differ.
gates.dataset_family: match: ADNI for both (P-33 ADNI-1 to 3; P-192 ADNI-GO/2), so subject overlap is likely.
gates.validation_tier: match: internal only (P-33 bootstrapped 20% test split; P-192 10-fold CV on CN/dementia then application to MCI).
gates.modality_family: mismatch: P-33 uses neuropsychological tests only; P-192's 68% PPV comes from CSF and PET biomarkers (its clinical-feature model gives 67.3%). The record's 'clinical_survey' fits P-33 only.

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: different endpoint (CU-to-MCI status vs MCI-to-dementia conversion at 4 years), different population (CU plus stable MCI with dementia converters excluded vs amnestic MCI including converters) and different metric type (ROC-AUC vs PPV).
performance_validity: flag does not apply: P-33's 0.96 is below 0.97 on a 1163-participant cohort; but the comparison is not a like-for-like performance comparison. Note P-33's inputs include CDRSB and MMSE, which enter the clinical diagnosis it predicts.
independence: Both draw on ADNI; P-33's ADNI-1 to 3 CU/MCI sample and P-192's ADNI-GO/2 aMCI sample probably overlap in part. Distinct authors.
grounds: The endpoints differ: P-33's AUC concerns CU vs MCI status (MCI onset) in a sample that excludes MCI-to-dementia converters, while P-192's PPV concerns MCI-to-dementia conversion at 4 years.
The metric types differ: a threshold-free ROC-AUC cannot be set against a prevalence-dependent PPV.
The predictor families differ (neuropsychological scores vs CSF/PET biomarkers), and the task gate fails with no waiver on record.

evidence_quotes.quote: MCI participants whose last visit indicated either reversion to CU or progression to dementia were excluded from the analysis to specifically characterize the transition from normal cognition to MCI.
The results show that Leaspy achieved the highest overall performance, with a top AUC of 0.96 and a composite criterion score of 68.7.
Area Under the Curve (AUC) of the Bayesian-KDE classifier at each visit, based on clinical diagnoses.

RUSBoost models applied to biomarker feature set provided > 35% improvement in the prediction of dementia over 2 years (model's PPV = 53.6 vs. observed rate of dementia onset = 18.0%) and > 45% over 4 years (model's PPV = 68% vs. observed rate of dementia onset = 22.2%).

We aimed to evaluate the value of ATN biomarker classification system (amyloid beta [A], pathologic tau [T], and neurodegeneration [N]) for predicting conversion from mild cognitive impairment (MCI) to dementia.

record_defects: task_equal 'Yes' is wrong: P-33's AUC is for the CU-to-MCI transition, P-192's PPV for MCI-to-dementia conversion.
modality_family 'clinical_survey' is wrong for P-192's 68% figure, which comes from the CSF/PET biomarker feature set.
validation_comparable 'Yes' and gap_magnitude 0.28 treat an AUC and a PPV as commensurable numbers.
The pack registry codes P-192 Best_Metric 'not reported' while the record uses 'PPV 68.0'; the paper does report PPV, sensitivity and specificity by horizon.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Only results on the same endpoint and metric (e.g. both papers reporting MCI-to-dementia AUC at a stated horizon in comparable ADNI samples) could be set against each other; these two papers do not provide them.
